requirement: Parse typed application settings from APP_ environment variables at call time with defaults and validation, and provide a pytest fixture that removes every APP_ variable through monkeypatch so each test starts from a clean, restored environment.
skeleton: A frozen Settings dataclass, load_settings parsing APP_PORT, APP_DEBUG and APP_HOSTS from os.environ with ValueError on bad input, and an app_env pytest fixture deleting prefixed variables via monkeypatch.
caption: Environment-driven configuration tested in isolation with the pytest monkeypatch fixture, using the standard-library os and dataclasses modules. Settings is a frozen dataclass of port, debug and hosts. load_settings() reads os.environ each time it is called, never at import. APP_PORT defaults to 8000; a value int cannot parse raises ValueError saying APP_PORT must be an integer with the repr of the raw text, raised from None, and a port outside 1 to 65535 inclusive raises ValueError saying it must be between those bounds. APP_DEBUG defaults to false, is stripped and lower-cased, must be one of 1, true, yes, on, 0, false, no or off, and otherwise raises ValueError saying APP_DEBUG must be a boolean. APP_HOSTS defaults to localhost and is split on commas with each name stripped and empty names dropped. The app_env fixture, declared with pytest.fixture and imported by test modules, takes monkeypatch, deletes every variable whose name starts with the APP_ prefix and returns monkeypatch so tests set values that are restored afterwards. The fixture asserts that with stray APP_PORT and APP_DEBUG removed the defaults are port 8000, debug False and localhost and no APP_ variable remains, that 65535, a padded TRUE and a host list with blanks parse correctly, that http, 0, 65536 and maybe raise ValueError with their messages, and that a changed APP_PORT is seen on the next call.

plan.intent: Test configuration parsing without leaking the developer's environment
constraints: Non-integer or out-of-range ports raise ValueError, with 65535 allowed
Debug flags are case-insensitive and unknown values raise ValueError
The fixture removes every APP_ variable, not just known ones
Settings are read when load_settings is called

rationale.teaches: Reading os.environ at call time and isolating tests with a monkeypatch-based fixture that clears a whole prefix.
rationale.why: A developer's exported variables leak into tests that only clear the names they know about, making suites pass locally and fail in CI or the reverse.

ops.docstring: Read APP_* settings from the environment, plus a fixture that isolates them.

candidates.why_wrong: Debug values are not stripped or lower-cased, so a padded TRUE is rejected.
The exclusive upper bound rejects port 65535, which is valid.
Empty names from trailing commas become empty host entries.
Only APP_PORT is removed, so any other stray APP_ variable leaks into the test.
The default port is 8080 instead of the documented 8000.
